title: Summer Bounty pechay (Summer Bounty F1): Characteristics
metaDescription: Summer Bounty pechay is an F1 hybrid pechay variety from Ramgo. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Summer Bounty pechay is an F1 hybrid pechay variety, also sold or known as Summer Bounty F1. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from Ramgo.

heroImage.alt: A farmer watering vegetable beds in Pulilan, Bulacan, the kind of farm where Summer Bounty pechay is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Summer Bounty F1, this is the same pechay. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [pechay variety finder](/crop-varieties/pechay), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [organic fertilizer for pechay](/blog/organic-fertilizer-for-pechay).
Key facts about Summer Bounty pechay

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

No day count or trial yield is published for this variety. So ask the seller or your municipal agriculturist for figures from farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit pechay fields most often: [bacterial soft rot](/diseases/soft-rot), [black rot of cabbage](/diseases/black-rot), [cabbage webworm](/pests/cabbage-webworm), [clubroot](/diseases/clubroot), [diamondback moth](/pests/diamondback-moth). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Days to harvest:** About 29 days after sowing (Ramgo).
**Fruit:** Leaves: green, fairly smooth, on a short plant about 14 cm tall.
Ramgo reports no bolting in its trials.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: one of Ramgo's Summer series of hybrid pechay (with Summer Plenty and Summer Wealthy), the only evidence found is Ramgo's own lineup. These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual pechay on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Summer Bounty pechay

Pechay is ready in about a month, so it fits small plots and quick cash. Pick a variety that bolts late in the heat and stands rain. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Summer Bounty F1 the same as Summer Bounty?
items.a: Yes. Summer Bounty F1 is another name for Summer Bounty. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
No. It is a hybrid, so seed saved from it does not grow true and yields less. Buy new seed each season.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Summer Bounty?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
